note: Encounters (Stage H, H.1; D-151): the ships that turn up on the scope, and how each behaves. `wants` is what it is looking for (H.2 gives its boarding party that goal). `at` is the kinds of point it can turn up at and `weight` how often. `signature` is what it gives off on its own course and burning after us: what our scope has to read. `sensors`, `reach`, `keen`, `notice` and `sure` are how hard it looks: our signature times `sensors`, falling to nothing at `reach`, has to pass `notice` before it takes an interest and `sure` before it is certain; `keen` is how fast it makes its mind up. `speed` is its cruise and its chase, against our 2.0 at full engine power (a stern chase closes only by the difference). `standoff` is how far off it shadows us, and `shadow` how many seconds it looks before it comes in anyway. `patience` is the seconds it will search with nothing to go on, and `chase` the seconds of pursuit before it gives up. `pings` (F.1, D-214) is how many times it will ping for a ship its search beam cannot find: a ping reads us better than the beam and shows us exactly where it is. Every contact is over in about a minute and a half (HUNT in src/sim/encounters.js), so `shadow`, `patience` and `chase` are short. `decoys` is how hard each kind of decoy pulls it (0 not at all; a ship that wants cargo takes a crate and goes). `bluffs` is the chance each lie works, before the crew's negotiation. `alongside` is the seconds before its clamp goes on and what it says first (a ship that boards needs it). `party` (H.2, src/sim/boarders.js) is who comes through the lock when it docks: how many, their names, skills and suits, what they say at the lock (`demand`; {crew_name} is the one a bounty is for, {system} what a wrecker wants), the `bribe` that sends them away from the lock, how many seconds they `stay` looking, how `thorough` a search is, and by goal: the `rooms` an inspection goes over with its `fine` and `faction`, the crates a raid means to `take`, and the systems a wrecker would `strip` first. H.3 (D-175 to D-177): `wants` may also be toll, hull or scan, for a ship that never docks and holds off at its `standoff` instead: a bulwark calls a `toll` ({ cost, zone, grace, demand }: credits, how close it calls, seconds to pay before its gun clears, what it says); a drone carrier swarms the hull with `drones` ({ every, max, total, fire, range }); a gunnery drone builds a `scan` of us ({ range, seconds, calls }) and calls in another encounter. `pods` ({ range, flight }) puts a boarding party across in pods that point defence can shoot down, instead of a clamp. `guns` ({ weapon, range, every, hit, warn, when }) is a gun it fires at our rooms: a weapon from content/weapons/, its reach in scope units, seconds between rounds, its chance to hit when it has us cold, how many warning shots come first, and when it opens up (running: we burn away while it closes; shot: we fired on it; closing: whenever it closes; toll: we have not paid). `nerve` is how much of our deterrent gun it takes to break off: a hit counts 1 and a warning shot 0.35; 0 or none means it never does. `radar` (F.2, D-218) is { reach, strength }: it reads our hull itself, however dark we run, as strongly as `strength` close in and falling to nothing at `reach`; going quiet does not hide us from it. Margo reads each kind's tells off its numbers once she has made it out (tellsOf).

items.name: Patrol cutter
items.blurb: Fast, well lit and by the book. It cannot be outrun, but its crew would rather read a clean manifest than open an airlock.

alongside.hail: Hauler, this is the cutter off your beam. Cut your drive and stand by your lock for inspection.

party.demand: Receivers customs. Three of us are coming through your lock to go over the hold. Keep your people out of our way.

items.name: Raider skiff
items.blurb: A hot, noisy drive on a small hull, after anything in a crate. It is slower than a hauler at full burn, and it will stop for cargo left in its path.

alongside.hail: Open your hold and nobody has to come looking for it.

party.demand: Two crates through the lock and we never came aboard. Make us look, and we take what we find.

items.name: Bounty tender
items.blurb: Runs cold and listens hard, for one name on a warrant. It does not clamp on: it stands off and fires its people across in pods, and it does not care what the manifest says.

alongside.hail: We hold a warrant for one of your crew. Pods are coming across. Send them to the lock and nobody else is touched.

party.demand: The warrant is for {crew_name}. Send them to the lock and nobody else is touched.

items.name: Scrap hauler
items.blurb: Slow, half blind and loud. It wants hull plate and fittings, ours if we look dead enough, and it will follow anything bright.

alongside.hail: No answer on any channel. Logging her as abandoned and making fast.

party.demand: Wrecker crew coming aboard to take her {system}. If anyone is alive in there, now is the time to say so.

items.name: Bulwark
items.blurb: All plating and patience, refitted as a toll gate. It is slow and it is armoured, our gun means nothing to it, and inside its zone it wants paying.

toll.demand: This lane is tolled. Sixty credits and you pass. Stay in our zone without paying and we will take it out of your hull.

items.name: Drone carrier
items.blurb: A survey tender whose drones learned to bite. It never comes close: it sits off and sends them to chew on the hull, and point defence is the answer.

items.name: Gunnery drone
items.blurb: Small, quick and unmanned. It shadows a ship until it has a good look, then calls in a patrol. One round puts it out of the sky.
